newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Schroeder backs French jobs programme.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Schroeder backs French jobs programme.

text.p: Gerhard Schroeder, a leading figure in Germany's opposition Social Democrats, said on Sunday he supported France's efforts to create more jobs in the European Union with an employment programme.
In an interview with the Handelsblatt newspaper to be published on Monday, Schroeder said Chancellor Helmut Kohl's centre-right government had blocked EU efforts to boost employment for too long.

"It is important that the employment chapter be filled with content and funding," said Schroeder, the premier of Lower Saxony and a leading candidate to challenge Kohl in the next general elections due in September 1998.

Schroeder, who stands alone on many issues in Germany, was the only leading German figure to speak out in favour of the employment programme. Kohl and most leaders said Germany was opposed to any such costly programmes, calling them obsolete.

"The federal government has been blocking this project long enough," Schroeder added, according to an advance release of the article. He said, however, Germany should not pay any additional amounts to the EU to funding the employment programme.
He said Germany should redirect funding it now contributes to the EU budget for the jobs schemes.
